column3: Trick number four reaches all the way into the mirror.
Researchers took photos of people, then used software to morph each face to look a little more attractive, or a little less, in small steps.
Weeks later, people had to pick their real photo out of the lineup.
On average, they picked a version that was slightly more attractive than the real one.
Not everyone did it, and the shift was small. But it pointed the same way. And people did it for close friends' faces too. Just not for strangers.
In another test, people spotted the flattering version of their own face faster than the less attractive one.
So your brain isn't only keeping secrets about the future. It's quietly retouching the present.
